Paragraph:
Translation: Here in this army there are many heroic bowmen equal in fighting to Bhima and Arjuna; there are also great fighters like Yuyudhana, Virata and Drupada.

Purport (Excerpt): Even though Dhrstadyumna was not a very important obstacle in the face of Dronacarya's very great power in the military art, there were many others who were the cause of fear. They are mentioned by Duryodhana as great stumbling blocks on the path of victory because each and every one of them was as formidable as Bhima and Arjuna. He knew the strength of Bhima and Arjuna, and thus he compared the others with them.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Duryodhana surveys the opposing forces and feels deeply intimidated by the presence of numerous elite warriors who are equal in strength to his most feared enemies, Bhima and Arjuna.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Duryodhana explicitly lists these formidable opponents to his commander, Dronacarya. He emphasizes the severity of the threat to ensure the enemy's strength is not underestimated.
Outcome/Resolution: He continues to mentally catalog the enemy's strengths, building a narrative of overwhelming opposition that reflects his internal dread.

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Bhaya (Existential fear stemming from a reliance on material power rather than righteousness)
Dvesha (Deep-seated aversion and animosity toward the enemy, amplifying the perception of threat)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: The verse illustrates a consciousness trapped in material calculation. Because Duryodhana's foundation is adharma (unrighteousness), he can only evaluate the situation through the lens of physical strength and military might, which inevitably results in a pervasive sense of fear.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Duryodhana is exhibiting a psychological state of hypervigilance and threat magnification. By measuring every opposing warrior against his ultimate fears (Bhima and Arjuna), he demonstrates a cognitive bias where anxiety causes him to perceive the opposing forces as overwhelmingly insurmountable 'stumbling blocks'.
